chunks: It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about two young feathered birds that I slaughtered while I was in Mecca. He said to me, “Why did you slaughter them?” I said: “A servant-girl from the people of Mecca brought them to me and asked me to slaughter them, and I thought that I was in Kufa and did not remember the Haram.” He said, “Give charity equal to their value.” I said, “How much?” He said, “One dirham, and it is better than them.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary whose sanctity was not remembered
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: one dirham, the amount specified as compensation
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the sacred city where the incident occurred
key_terms.مُسَرْوَلَيْنِ: feathered or fledged, describing the birds

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone slaughters small birds in the Haram of Mecca by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning killing young birds within the Haram of Mecca. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that compensation be given as charity according to their value, specifying one dirham in this case, showing the sanctity of the Haram and the obligation of financial redress for the violation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2372 - Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj narrated:

"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about two young birds dressed in feathers that I slaughtered while I was in Mecca.
Imam (as) said to me: 'Why did you slaughter them?'
I replied: 'A girl from the people of Mecca brought them to me and asked me to slaughter them, and I thought I was in Kufa and did not recall the sanctity of the Haram.'
Imam (as) said: 'Give charity equivalent to their value.'
I asked: 'How much?'
Imam (as) said: 'A dirham, which is better than them.'"
